mainTopic: Burning אימורים after the afternoon תמיד on ערב פסח, and a קרבן פסח offered שלא לשמו.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a דרשה: the מצורע's עולה counts even if it was offered before his חטאת. The גמרא then challenges רב פפא's ruling that on ערב פסח, after the afternoon תמיד, a מחוסר כפורים may bring his offerings and leave the אימורים overnight on the מזבח. רב פפא answers the first challenge with the principle כהנים זריזין הן. A second challenge argues that without burning the אימורים the כהנים cannot eat, and without their eating the owner has no כפרה. The answer is that blocked אימורים are treated like ones that became טמא or were lost, and a ברייתא proves this. Next come two contradictions between פסוקים about fats staying overnight. רב כהנא resolves his own by saying the night is for leftover fats. For רב ספרא's question, רב quotes an answer limiting the פסוק to a year when the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת. Finally a new משנה teaches that a קרבן פסח offered שלא לשמו, even with mixed intent, is פסול. רב פפא asks whether that mixed intent was in one עבודה or two, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse shows the leper's burnt-offering works even if already offered first
steps.stepSummary: The verse about the מצורע's עולה is read in the past tense: an עולה that was already offered still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the priest shall offer the burnt-offering" means a burnt-offering that he already offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof from a פסוק that started on the previous amud. The verse is read to mean that the מצורע's עולה works even if it was brought before his חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the חטאת comes before the עולה. The verse's wording "והעלה" is read as "he already offered it." This teaches that the מצורע still gets his כפרה even if the order was reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, burned entirely on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an argument from the previous section, not the start of a new topic. Do not read it as a fresh opening.

phrases.english: "And the priest shall offer the burnt-offering"
— meaning one that he has already offered.
phrases.notes: Reads the verb as describing something already done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a derivation that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That the מצורע's עולה is valid even if it was offered before the חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא יד:כ, read as "which he already offered."

steps.title: Leaving the fats overnight on the altar could trick the priests
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא challenges רב פפא: leaving the אימורים overnight on top of the מזבח invites a mistake, because כהנים may think they are from today and burn them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said to רב פפא: According to you, who said he brings the fats up and leaves them overnight on top of the מזבח, are we really going to set up a situation where the כהנים could stumble? They might think the fats are from today's offerings and come to burn them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמן בר אבא attacks רב פפא's ruling. Putting the fats on the מזבח without burning them could cause the כהנים to burn them by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had ruled that after the afternoon תמיד, the אימורים are not burned that day. Instead they are brought up and left on top of the מזבח overnight. The problem is that fats lying on the מזבח look like today's fats that should be burned, which creates a תקלה.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings it up and leaves it overnight
A mishap, a stumbling into error

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said to Rav Pappa:
According to you, who said
he brings them up and leaves them overnight at the top of the altar,
do we stand and do something for the priests
through which they will come to a mishap?
For they will think it is from that day
and they will come to burn it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא לְדִידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to challenge רב פפא's practical ruling from the earlier discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that the אימורים are brought up and left overnight on top of the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fats sitting on the מזבח will look like today's fats, so כהנים may burn them at the wrong time.

steps.title: Priests are careful and will not make that mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that כהנים are זריזין, so there is no real worry of a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Priests are careful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. כהנים are trusted to be alert, so they will not burn the leftover fats by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about a תקלה assumed the כהנים might be careless. רב פפא rejects that assumption: כהנים are known for being careful and will warn one another. So his ruling stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle כהנים זריזין הן comes up in many places in שס to explain why we do not worry that כהנים will make mistakes.

phrases.english: He said to him: Priests are careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenge's assumption that a mistake is likely.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving the fats on the מזבח would lead כהנים to burn them by mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים are careful, so there is no real concern and רב פפא's ruling stands.

steps.title: Priests may not eat the meat until the fats are burned
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge to רב פפא begins: as long as the אימורים are not burned, the כהנים cannot eat the meat. This is proven from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא (and some say רב הונא בריה דרב נתן said to רב פפא): But as long as the אימורים have not been burned, the כהנים cannot eat the meat! As it was taught: I might think the כהנים may take the חזה ושוק before the אימורים are burned. So the פסוק says, "And the כהן shall burn the חלב on the מזבח," and only after that, "and the breast shall be for אהרן and his sons."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second attack on רב פפא. This is the first link of the attack: if the fats are left unburned until tomorrow, the כהנים cannot eat the meat today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the order of the פסוק that burning the חלב must come before the כהנים get the חזה ושוק. So delaying the burning also delays the eating. This step only sets up the problem; the punchline comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it (another version of who said it)
The parts of an offering burned on the altar
Breast and thigh, the כהנים' portion of a שלמים

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said it to Rav Pappa:
But isn't it so that as long as the sacrificial parts have not been burned
the priests cannot eat the meat?
As it was taught: I might think the priests would be permitted
to eat the breast and thigh before the burning of the sacrificial parts.

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַחֵלֶב הַמִּזְבֵּחָה״,
phrases.english: So the verse says: "And the priest shall burn the fat on the altar,"
and only then: "And the breast shall be for Aaron and his sons."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כַּמָּה דְּלָא מִתְקַטְּרִי אֵמוּרִין כֹּהֲנִים לָא מָצוּ אָכְלִי בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new and different challenge to רב פפא begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that the אימורים are left unburned overnight.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fats are not burned today, the כהנים cannot eat the meat today. This prepares the next link in step 5.

steps.title: The owner is not atoned until the priests eat
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is completed: until the כהנים eat, the owner has no כפרה. So the מחוסר כפורים cannot be atoned today and cannot eat his פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as long as the priests have not eaten the meat, the owners are not atoned. As it was taught: "And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made" teaches that the priests eat, and through that the owners are atoned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the second link and finishes the challenge to רב פפא. If the כהנים cannot eat until tomorrow, the owner is not atoned today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the full chain: the fats are not burned today, so the כהנים cannot eat today, so the owner has no כפרה today. A מחוסר כפורים needs his כפרה in order to eat the קרבן פסח. So how can רב פפא's ruling help him on ערב פסח? The answer comes next.
steps.whatToRemember: Remember the chain of three: (1) burn the אימורים, then (2) the כהנים eat, then (3) the owner is atoned. Leaving the fats overnight breaks the chain for today.
steps.confusionAlert: The כהנים eating is not just their reward. According to this ברייתא, their eating is part of what completes the owner's כפרה.

phrases.english: And as long as the priests have not eaten the meat
the owners are not atoned,
as it was taught: "And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made,"
this teaches that the priests eat
and the owners are atoned!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה דְּכֹהֲנִים לָא אָכְלִי בָּשָׂר בְּעָלִים לָא מִתְכַּפְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second link that turns step 4 into a full challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the מחוסר כפורים can be atoned in time on ערב פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No burning means no eating by the כהנים, and no eating means no כפרה. So the person stays a מחוסר כפורים and cannot eat the פסח.

steps.title: Unburnable אימורים are treated like lost or impure ones
steps.stepSummary: The one who was challenged answers (רב כהנא, or in the other version רב פפא): since the אימורים cannot be burned, they are treated as if they became טמא or were lost, so the כהנים may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since it is impossible to burn them, the אימורים were treated like ones that became טמא or were lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The one who was challenged (רב כהנא, or in the other version רב פפא) answers the challenge from steps 4-5. Since the אימורים cannot be burned now, the כהנים are allowed to eat the meat anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said the כהנים cannot eat until the אימורים are burned, so the owner never gets כפרה. The answer is that this rule only applies when burning is possible. Here the burning is blocked, so it is like a case where the אימורים are טמא or lost, and in that case the meat may be eaten. Once the meat is eaten, the owner has his כפרה and can eat his פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) made them / treated them as

phrases.english: He said to him: Since it is impossible
phrases.notes: Burning is blocked by the rule of השלמה, which says nothing is burned after the afternoon תמיד.

phrases.english: they rendered them like ones that became impure or were lost.
phrases.notes: So the כהנים may eat even though the אימורים were not burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that the owner cannot get כפרה because the כהנים cannot eat.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: blocked burning is treated like the known case of impure or lost אימורים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Unburned אימורים always stop the כהנים from eating the meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the burning is impossible, the כהנים eat anyway, and the owner gets כפרה.

steps.title: ברייתא: the כהנים get the breast and thigh in any case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that even when the אימורים are טמא or lost, the כהנים still receive the חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: I might think that if the אימורים became טמא or were lost, the כהנים would not be entitled to the breast and thigh. Therefore the פסוק says: 'And the breast shall be for אהרן and his sons', meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the rule relied on in step 6's answer. If the אימורים are lost or טמא, the כהנים still get their portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהנים eat only after the אימורים are burned. The ברייתא learns from 'והיה החזה לאהרן ולבניו' that the gift belongs to the כהנים no matter what happens to the אימורים. This is the source for treating unburnable אימורים the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
The breast and thigh, the כהנים' portion of a שלמים
In any case / no matter what

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל נִטְמְאוּ אֵמוּרִין אוֹ שֶׁאָבְדוּ
phrases.english: As it was taught: I might think that if the sacrificial parts became impure or were lost,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ כֹּהֲנִים זַכָּאִין בְּחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק —
phrases.english: the priests would not be entitled to the breast and thigh.
The verse states: 'And the breast shall be for Aaron and his sons,'
in any event.
phrases.notes: The gift does not depend on the אימורים being burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule used in step 6's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהנים may eat even when the אימורים are not burned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא learning from 'והיה החזה לאהרן ולבניו' (ויקרא ז:לא).
steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים' right to the חזה ושוק does not depend on the אימורים actually being burned. So the מחוסר כפורים can still get his כפרה and eat his פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the challenge against רב פפא, and his position stands.

steps.title: רב כהנא's contradiction: fats overnight versus completing everything before the afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק suggests fats may stay all night. Another פסוק teaches that all offerings must be finished before the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא raised a contradiction. It is written: 'The fat of My festival offering shall not remain until morning.' That means it may not remain until morning, but it may remain the whole night. Yet it is written: 'And he shall burn upon it the fats of the שלמים', which teaches: upon it (the תמיד) complete all the offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא points out two פסוקים that seem to clash. One allows fats to be burned through the night. The other requires everything to be finished by the afternoon תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not until morning' implies the fats may be burned anytime during the night. But the rule of השלמה says the afternoon תמיד must be the last offering of the day. So how can fats be burned after it, at night?

keyTerms.meaning: He threw together, meaning he raised a contradiction
The fat parts burned on the מזבח
Complete: finish all the offerings before the afternoon תמיד

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised a contradiction: It is written
'The fat of My festive offering shall not remain until morning'
so it is until morning that it may not remain,
but it may remain the entire night.
And it is written: 'And he shall burn upon it the fats of the peace offerings'
upon it complete all the offerings!
phrases.notes: 'Upon it' refers to the תמיד, so nothing is offered after the afternoon תמיד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related discussion about burning fats after the afternoon תמיד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about when fats may be burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק implies fats may be burned all night. The other demands that everything be completed before the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: Answer: the first פסוק speaks of leftover fats
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers his own question: fats may be burned at night only when they were left over and not burned in time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the question and he answered it: the פסוק is speaking of fats that were left over.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא resolves his own contradiction. Ideally everything is finished before the afternoon תמיד, but fats that were left over may still be burned all night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are true, but at different levels. השלמה is the ideal plan. 'Not until morning' teaches that if fats were left over, they may still be burned through the night.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ,
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
when they were left over.
phrases.notes: The fats were not burned before the afternoon תמיד.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: ideal procedure versus leftover fats after the fact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים contradict each other about burning fats at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: השלמה is the ideal plan. Leftover fats may still be burned until morning.
steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not saying the rule of השלמה can be ignored. Burning at night is only for fats that were already left over.
steps.whatToRemember: השלמה is the ideal rule, but leftover fats may be burned all night until morning.

steps.title: רב ספרא's contradiction: פסח fats overnight versus no weekday offering on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק implies the פסח fats may be burned all night, which is יום טוב. But 'עולת שבת בשבתו' forbids weekday offerings on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא raised a contradiction before רב. It is written: 'The offering of the פסח festival shall not remain until morning.' That means not until morning, but it may remain the whole night. Yet it is written: 'The עולה of שבת on its שבת', meaning not a weekday עולה on שבת, and not a weekday עולה on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new contradiction between two פסוקים. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח is slaughtered on ערב פסח, a weekday, so its fats are part of a weekday offering. The first פסוק implies those fats may be burned during the night, which is already יום טוב. But 'עולת שבת בשבתו' teaches that a weekday offering may not be brought on שבת or יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The שבת עולה on its own שבת

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְרַב: כְּתִיב
phrases.english: Rav Safra raised a contradiction before Rav: It is written
'The sacrifice of the feast of Passover shall not remain until morning'
so it is until morning that it may not remain,
but it may remain all night.
But it is written: 'The burnt offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat'
and not a weekday burnt offering on Shabbat,
and not a weekday burnt offering on a Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel contradiction in the same style as רב כהנא's, now about the פסח fats on the night of יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that the פסח fats may be burned on the night of יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning weekday fats on יום טוב breaks the rule learned from 'עולת שבת בשבתו'.

steps.title: The verse speaks about the fourteenth of ניסן falling on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב answers by quoting רבי אבהו: the פסוק about the fats staying all night refers to a year when the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת. The fats of שבת offerings may be offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב אבא בר חייא already asked this contradiction to רבי אבהו, and he answered him: Here we are dealing with a case where the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, because the fats of שבת offerings may be offered on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the contradiction from Step 10. He says this exact question was already asked, and he quotes the answer רבי אבהו gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the fats of a weekday offering may not be burned on יום טוב, yet the פסוק lets the פסח fats burn through the night of יום טוב. The answer limits the פסוק to a year when the קרבן פסח was brought on שבת. Fats of a שבת offering may be burned on יום טוב, so in that case there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised it as a contradiction (set two sources against each other)
The fourteenth of ניסן, the day the קרבן פסח is slaughtered
The fats of offerings brought on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this answer allows every weekday offering's fats on יום טוב. The point is that when ערב פסח is שבת, the פסח was a שבת offering. Only the fats of שבת offerings may be burned on יום טוב.

phrases.english: He (רב) said to him: Already raised this contradiction before
phrases.notes: רב is answering רב ספרא's question from Step 10.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַבָּא בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: Rav Abba bar Chiyya, to Rabbi Abbahu,
and he answered him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with the fourteenth of Nisan that falls on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פסוק that lets the fats stay on the מזבח all night.

phrases.english: because the fats of Shabbat offerings may be offered on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the פסוק is set in a special calendar situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to allow weekday פסח fats to burn on the night of יום טוב, against 'עולת שבת בשבתו'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks only of a year when the fourteenth falls on שבת. Those are שבת fats, and they may be burned on יום טוב.

steps.title: Should the whole verse be limited to such a rare case?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא objects: just because שבת fats may be offered on יום טוב, should we say the whole פסוק was written only for the rare year when the fourteenth falls on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because the fats of שבת may be offered on יום טוב, shall we stand up and say that this פסוק was written only about the fourteenth that falls on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא challenges the answer רב quoted in Step 11. He finds it hard to accept that a general פסוק talks only about an unusual year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that שבת fats may be burned on יום טוב is correct. The objection is about reading the פסוק. The פסוק sounds like a general law for every year, so limiting it to a rare calendar case feels forced.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we stand up and say (a rhetorical way of protesting a reading)

phrases.english: He (Rav Safra) said to him: Because the fats of Shabbat
may be offered on a Festival,
shall we stand up and say about it
that this verse, about the fourteenth
that falls on Shabbat, is the case it was written for?
phrases.notes: This is a question in form, but it works as a challenge to the answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן נֵיקוּ וְנֵימָא לֵיהּ דְּהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's limited reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general פסוק should not be confined to a rare calendar case just because a rule allows that case.

steps.title: The verse forces itself into this case
steps.stepSummary: רב answers: leave the פסוק alone. The contradiction itself forces us to explain it this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave the פסוק alone, because it pushes itself and sets itself up in this case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends the limited reading. The two sources clash, and only this reading makes them fit, so we must accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב agrees the reading is narrow but says there is no other choice. 'עולת שבת בשבתו' forbids weekday fats on יום טוב, so the only way the פסוק works is in the שבת case. This ends the discussion about the fats.

keyTerms.meaning: Establishes itself (the verse explains its own case)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק that lets the פסח fats burn all night on יום טוב refers to a year when ערב פסח is שבת. Then the fats are שבת fats, which may be burned on יום טוב. The contradiction forces this reading.

phrases.english: He (רב) said to him: Leave the verse alone,
since it forces itself and establishes itself in this case.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁבְקֵיהּ לִקְרָא, דְּהוּא דָּחֵיק וּמוֹקֵים אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection of Step 12 and keeps the answer of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Forced reading: the contradiction requires the limited case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Limiting the פסוק to a rare case looked too narrow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without that limit the פסוק contradicts 'עולת שבת בשבתו', so the פסוק itself requires it.

steps.title: A קרבן פסח offered with the wrong intent is invalid
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a קרבן פסח was slaughtered, or its blood received, carried, or sprinkled, with intent for a different offering, or with mixed intent, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A קרבן פסח that was slaughtered not for its own purpose, or whose blood was received, carried, or sprinkled not for its own purpose, or for its own purpose and not for its own purpose, or not for its own purpose and for its own purpose, is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It teaches that wrong intent during any of the four main blood steps invalidates the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four key acts: slaughtering, receiving the blood, carrying it, and sprinkling it. If the כהן thinks of a different קרבן during any of them, the פסח is פסול. Even mixed intent, where only part of the thought is wrong, invalidates it.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own purpose (intending it as a different קרבן)
Received the blood in a vessel
Carried the blood to the מזבח
Sprinkled the blood on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is still a קרבן פסח. The wrong intent only makes this particular one invalid. Also, one wrong-intent act is enough. It does not need wrong intent in all four acts.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule of קדשים: the כהן's intent can disqualify a קרבן. For the קרבן פסח, wrong intent invalidates it completely.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered not for its own purpose,
or received, carried, or sprinkled the blood not for its own purpose,
phrases.notes: Each of these acts on its own is enough to disqualify the פסח.

phrases.english: or for its own purpose and not for its own purpose,
or not for its own purpose and for its own purpose —
it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the fats discussion ended in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wrong or mixed intent in slaughtering, receiving, carrying, or sprinkling makes a קרבן פסח פסול.

steps.title: What 'mixed intent' means
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines its terms. 'For its purpose and not for its purpose' means first thinking פסח, then שלמים. 'Not for its purpose and for its purpose' means first thinking שלמים, then פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is 'for its purpose and not for its purpose'? For the sake of a פסח and for the sake of a שלמים. 'Not for its purpose and for its purpose' means for the sake of a שלמים and for the sake of a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks itself what the two mixed-intent cases mean, and then explains each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is only the order of the thoughts. In the first case the correct intent (פסח) comes first and the wrong one (שלמים) follows. In the second the wrong one comes first. Either order makes the קרבן פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of a קרבן פסח
Peace-offering, a different type of קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: A קרבן פסח is פסול if the wrong intent comes at any of the four blood steps. This is true even when it is mixed with the right intent, whichever comes first.

phrases.english: How is 'for its own purpose and not for its own purpose'?
For the sake of a Paschal lamb and for the sake of a peace-offering.
'Not for its own purpose and for its own purpose' —
for the sake of a peace-offering and for the sake of a Paschal lamb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two mixed-intent cases listed in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed intent means thinking of both פסח and שלמים, in either order, and both orders invalidate the פסח.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: one rite or two rites?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the משנה's case of mixed intent, 'for the פסח and not for the פסח', is about one עבודה or about two separate עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב פפא asked: Did we learn the משנה about one עבודה, or did we learn it about two עבודות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a question from רב פפא. He wants to know how to picture the mixed-intent case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that 'for its purpose and not for its purpose' makes the פסח פסול. רב פפא asks whether the כהן had both thoughts during one act, like the שחיטה. The other possibility is that he had one thought during one act and the other thought during a different act, like the זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that begins after the משנה
He asked; he raised a question he was unsure about
One of the four main Temple acts: שחיטה, receiving the blood, carrying it, or sprinkling it

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two עבודות' does not mean two animals. It is the same קרבן פסח, with one thought during one act and a different thought during another act.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא on the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Did we learn it about one rite,
phrases.notes: For example, both thoughts during the slaughtering

phrases.english: or did we learn it about two rites?
phrases.notes: One thought during one act, the other thought during another act

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה quoted in steps 14 and 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the mixed intent in the משנה happened within one עבודה or across two עבודות.

steps.title: If it is one rite, the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the first possibility. If the case is one עבודה, the משנה must follow רבי יוסי, who holds that even the end of a person's words counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we learned it about one עבודה, then the משנה follows רבי יוסי, who said: a person is held even to the end of his words.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins to explain why his question matters. He shows what follows if the case is one עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a כהן who says during the שחיטה, 'for the פסח and for שלמים.' The משנה calls it פסול, so the second half of his words must count. That matches רבי יוסי's view that a person is held to the end of his words, not only the beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that the end of a person's words also counts
The end of his words; what he says after his first words
Is held to; is bound by

phrases.english: If we learned it about one rite,
then it is Rabbi Yosei, who said:
a person is held even to the end of his words.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי counts both halves, so the second, wrong thought ruins the offering

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲבוֹדָה אַחַת תְּנַן וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops the first side of רב פפא's question by tying it to a תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Showing that the one-עבודה reading forces the משנה to follow רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Why it cannot be רבי מאיר: only the first words count
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains why the one-עבודה reading cannot follow רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר holds that we go by the first words only.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it were רבי מאיר, he said: hold on to the first words.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the reason the one-עבודה reading must follow רבי יוסי. רבי מאיר could not call this offering פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says that when a person's words conflict, only his first words count. A כהן who said 'for the פסח and for שלמים' started with 'פסח,' so רבי מאיר would treat it as a proper פסח and call it כשר. Since the משנה calls it פסול, the one-עבודה reading cannot fit רבי מאיר. The second side of the question, two עבודות, continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that only a person's first words count
Hold on to the first words; what he said first is what counts

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about how to read a person's words, such as declaring an animal 'עולה and שלמים.' רב פפא applies that argument to a כהן's thoughts during the עבודה.

phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Meir —
surely he said: hold on to the first words,
phrases.notes: So 'for the פסח' would count, and the offering would be כשר

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָא אָמַר תְּפוֹס לָשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind step 17: רבי מאיר's view cannot produce a פסול ruling in a one-עבודה case.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the one-עבודה reading must follow רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's rule of תפוס לשון ראשון, which would make the offering כשר.
